heat.curveEditor.hint: Double-click to add a point, alt-click or right-click one to remove it. Drag the small circles to bend each segment. The endpoints are fixed at the centre and the rim; their height is still yours.
heat.curveEditor.presetTitle: Replace the curve with the {preset} preset
heat.rampEditor.position: Position along the ramp (0 = no heat)
heat.timeline.window.cumulativeTitle: Everything from the start of the data up to the playhead — heat builds up as it plays
heat.timeline.window.fixedTitle: A fixed span of history ending at the playhead
heat.timeline.window.lifetimeTitle: Each datapoint lives until the same person's next sample, so one current position per person. Points with no next sample use the fallback lifetime.
heat.timeline.allTitle: Show every datapoint at once, ignoring the playhead
heat.timeline.playTitle: Play the data as a timelapse
heat.timeline.historyTitle: What counts as visible at the playhead
heat.timeline.spanTitle: Length of the visible span ending at the playhead
heat.timeline.fallbackLifeTitle: How long a datapoint stays visible when that person never appears again — a death, a disconnect, or the end of the log.
heat.timeline.fadeTitle: Fraction of each datapoint's life spent fading out. Without it a datapoint vanishes between one frame and the next, which reads as a flicker rather than as something ending — and with one sample live per person the whole field flickers at the sample rate.
heat.timeline.noDataset: No dataset — drop a folder of {formats} in the sidebar, or generate one
heat.sessionPicker.allHint: Every session at once. Positions are still never interpolated across a session boundary, but concurrent matches put unrelated players on the map together — pick one to play a match back.
heat.sessionPicker.seekHint: In the heat modes this only moves the playhead to the session's start; the heat still counts every session. Box replay plays the chosen session alone.
heat.softwareRenderingWarning.title: Running without the graphics card.
heat.speedOverlay.title: Camera fly speed. Drag up or down to change it — further is faster, Shift for fine. The mouse wheel over the viewport does the same thing in steps.
heat.cameraPose.copyTitle: Copy this viewpoint to the clipboard
heat.cameraPose.hint: {key} or blur applies. Values follow the camera while not focused.
heat.datasetPanel.title: Dataset
heat.datasetPanel.summary: {teams, plural, one {# team} other {# teams}} · {persons, plural, one {# person} other {# persons}} · {span}s span
heat.datasetPanel.syntheticHint: Battle-royale-shaped movement: teams drop apart, then converge. Gives a realistic density distribution to tune against.
heat.datasetPanel.memory: ≈ {ram} GB of RAM, {gpu} GB on the GPU after quantisation.
heat.entityPanel.title: Entities
heat.entityPanel.hint: Shows only the selected entities, in the heat as in the box replay. Leave empty to show everyone.
heat.entityPanel.noSlot: Not applied to the heat: all filter slots are taken. The box replay still shows only these entities. Clear a filter under Filters to free one.
heat.entityPanel.matchesFirst: {count, plural, one {# match} other {# matches}}, showing the first {page}
heat.entityPanel.onlyShownTitle: Select only what is currently listed
heat.filterPanel.title: Filters
heat.filterPanel.noColumns: No columns were retained for filtering. Pick some under “{label}” in the column mapping before loading — they have to be read at ingest time.
heat.filterPanel.overflow: Only the first {count, plural, one {# filter is} other {# filters are}} applied. Clear one — the rest are being ignored, not silently combined.
heat.filterPanel.hint: Applied in the shader, so these take effect on the next frame at any dataset size.
heat.filterPanel.personSlot: The Entities selection takes one of these slots.
heat.heatPanel.nothingToMeter: nothing lit to meter — used the analytic estimate
heat.heatPanel.metered: metered {coverage}% of the frame; 98th percentile {reference} placed near the top of the ramp
heat.heatPanel.radiusHint: World-space radius of each sprite. Sprites always face the camera, so this shrinks with distance.
heat.heatPanel.edgeIntensityHint: Heat at the sprite's outer rim. Negative values carve cool halos around hot spots.
heat.heatPanel.falloffTitle: One exponent, optionally S-curved. Faster to dial in.
heat.heatPanel.curveTitle: Draw the cross-section of a sprite as a Bézier — plateaus, shelves and rings that no single exponent can express.
heat.heatPanel.falloffHint: 1 is a straight linear ramp. Higher tightens the hotspot toward the centre.
heat.heatPanel.smoothRampTitle: S-curve the ramp so a sprite fades in at its rim instead of ending on a visible edge.
heat.heatPanel.saturationHint: Accumulated heat that maps to the top of the ramp. Applied at composite, so dragging this never restarts convergence.
heat.heatPanel.floorHint: Every pixel carrying any heat at all is lifted to at least this point on the ramp, so a single datapoint shows up instead of sitting just above transparent. Turn it up and the radius down to see individual points; leave it off to judge density.
heat.heatPanel.saturatingTitle: Approaches the top of the ramp asymptotically, the way stacked translucent sprites do. Nothing ever goes flat white.
heat.heatPanel.linearTitle: Equal colour means equal count. The only honest choice when comparing two datasets or two time windows.
heat.heatPanel.logTitle: Compresses a long tail, so one extreme hotspot stops flattening everything else to the bottom of the ramp.
heat.heatPanel.flattenTitle: Ignore each row's height and stack all heat on the floor — the classic 2D map heatmap.
heat.heatPanel.teamsHint: One hue per group, from the circle divided into {count, plural, one {# equal part} other {# equal parts}}, with each group taking the centre of its slice — so any two are as far apart as the count allows and opposites stay opposite. Where groups overlap the hues mix, and an even contest comes out neutral. The ramp below still sets the opacity, so density reads exactly as it does in the other modes.
heat.heatPanel.separationHint: How far a mixture is pushed from neutral. 0 makes everything grey; 1 is the true average; past 2 the brightest mixtures clamp.
heat.heatPanel.opacityRamp: Opacity ramp (colour comes from the group)
heat.heatPanel.resetPositive: Reset to transparent → red → yellow → white
heat.heatPanel.resetNegative: Reset to transparent → green → blue → purple
heat.heatPanel.clampsHint: The overdraw guard. A sprite covering N pixels costs N blend operations, so an unclamped radius up close is what turns a 60fps frame into a 2fps one.
heat.heatPanel.minPixelRadiusHint: Keeps distant data from vanishing below one pixel.
heat.heatPanel.depthHint: How much a datapoint behind the level is suppressed. Without this the heat is a flat overlay: everything glows through every wall at full strength, the depth the level provides is cancelled out, and a hotspot inside a building looks the same as one on its roof.
heat.heatPanel.hideBehindTerrainTitle: Drop datapoints standing behind the ground entirely, instead of dimming them. Terrain and walls are opaque in different ways: you look through a wall on purpose, to see which floor the traffic was on, and never through a hill — behind one is the far side of the map, which has no depth cue to place it and sums along the horizon into a band brighter than the foreground.
heat.heatPanel.occlusionHint: Compared per pixel against the level's depth, and compounded per surface, so a room four walls deep is fainter than a corridor one wall in. At 1 the points behind a wall are not drawn at all, which is also the cheapest setting. With the terrain cutoff above on, this is about walls only.
heat.heatPanel.groundProjectedHint: Ground-projected mode flattens every datapoint onto one plane, so there is no depth left to compare — occlusion is off while it is on.
heat.heatPanel.cullingHint: Restricts the splat to a shell around the camera. Set a far bound to read density inside a building without the far side of the map summing on top of it; set a near bound to fly through a hotspot instead of into it. Both are evaluated in the vertex shader, so a culled row costs no fragments at all.
heat.heatPanel.cutPlaneTitle: Measure the bounds along the view axis instead of from the eye, so the cut is a plane parallel to the screen rather than a sphere around you. A sphere's edge curves away across the frame and slides whenever you turn; a plane stays where you put it.
heat.heatPanel.cutLevelTitle: Cut the ground, structures and water at the same bounds, not only the heat. With the level left whole the plane removes the datapoints and leaves the building standing in front of them, which hides what the plane was moved there to show; with both cut it is a section through the map and the points sit against the walls and floors they belong to.
heat.heatPanel.cullKeys: <kbd>{closer}</kbd> and <kbd>{further}</kbd> push the far plane in and out while you fly, and <kbd>{toggle}</kbd> turns it off and on again at the distance you left it — so you can walk it through a building rather than set it once.
heat.levelPanel.downscaled: Downscaled from {sourceWidth}×{sourceHeight} to {width}×{height} — {max}px is the largest edge the GPU will hold.
heat.levelPanel.splitWater: Ground {ground}, structures {structures}, water {water} across {parts} of {total, plural, one {# part} other {# parts}}.
heat.levelPanel.split: Ground {ground}, structures {structures} across {parts} of {total, plural, one {# part} other {# parts}}.
heat.levelPanel.importedAtSuggest: Imported at {lod} — large enough that {suggested} would be worth trying.
heat.levelPanel.encodeFailed: Could not encode the map image.
heat.levelPanel.saved: Saved. It will load instantly next time.
heat.levelPanel.entryGone: That entry is no longer in the library.
heat.levelPanel.entryEmpty: That entry has no usable payload.
heat.levelPanel.title: Background / level
heat.levelPanel.nothingLoaded: Nothing loaded — the scene shows a grid and axes. Add a map image or a level mesh to give the heat context.
heat.levelPanel.dotaTitle: The Dota 2 map as OpenDota draws it, fetched from opendota.com and placed in Dota world units under tables from the Watcher's Dota 2 replays
heat.levelPanel.dotaFailed: Could not fetch the Dota 2 map: {reason}
heat.levelPanel.dotaNotice: Map drawing by OpenDota (opendota.com). Dota 2 and its map belong to Valve, who do not endorse this project.
heat.levelPanel.simplificationHint: Applied when a model is imported. Edge-collapse with quadric error, so silhouettes and hard edges survive — level geometry is a backdrop and does not need its full triangle count. Accepts {extensions}.
heat.levelPanel.desaturateHint: Grey background, saturated heat. Colour in the map competes with colour in the data.
heat.levelPanel.reliefHint: Terrain normals nearly all point up, so a light alone gives it one flat grey and a valley looks like a plateau. Contours are the cue that survives however shallow the ground is; slope darkening and the elevation ramp carry the large-scale shape.
heat.levelPanel.slopeHint: Darkens by steepness, so banks and cliffs read from any camera angle.
heat.levelPanel.elevationRampHint: Low ground darker, high ground lighter.
heat.levelPanel.waterTitle: Lakes, rivers and the sea, drawn flat: none of the terrain cues apply to a surface that is level by definition.
heat.levelPanel.groundTrianglesHint: The terrain's own edges, drawn over the shaded surface. Shows how coarsely the ground was sampled, and turns a smooth shaded slope into something you can judge distances on. Built on first use, which takes a moment on a large level.
heat.levelPanel.wireframeTitle: Replace the terrain surface with its edges. Fully schematic — and it gives up the shading, the contours and the occlusion, so the slider above is usually what you want.
heat.levelPanel.groundTextureTitle: Draw the ground with the texture the file carries. An extracted racetrack carries one per tile, at 25 cm a pixel: asphalt, verge, grass and woodland, which the geometry alone cannot show. Brightness still applies, which is the way to quieten it under the heat.
heat.levelPanel.colourTitle: Shade the ground with the colour the scan captured, instead of grey. A reconstructed racetrack is one flat ribbon flowing into its surroundings, and shading alone does not tell the road from the verge beside it. Turn it off to go back to the grey map the heat reads against — the relief shading and contours stay on either way.
heat.levelPanel.noColour: This level carries no colour. Engine exports have none; a scan from the game-capture exporter does.
heat.levelPanel.structuresTextured: Barriers, kerbs, signs and props, drawn solid in their own textures.
heat.levelPanel.structuresShell: Buildings and props, drawn as a transparent shell so you can see the heat inside them.
heat.levelPanel.structureParts: {parts} of {total, plural, one {# part} other {# parts}}.
heat.levelPanel.structureTextureTitle: Draw structures solid, in the textures and colours they were exported with - an extracted racetrack's guardrails, tyre walls, kerbs and signs. Off draws them as the tinted see-through shell instead, which shows heat behind and inside them.
heat.levelPanel.shellFacesTitle: A faint surface with a bright rim, so a building reads as a volume rather than a cage.
heat.levelPanel.faceOpacityHint: Keep this low. Solid structures hide the data inside them, which is the thing you are looking at.
heat.levelPanel.sharpEdgesTitle: Shade each triangle by its own normal. Exported levels are welded, so the averaged normals round off every corner and a row of boxes reads as a heap of foil. Turn off for a level whose curved surfaces matter more than its corners.
heat.levelPanel.placementHint: Two anchors: a pixel on the image and the world coordinate it sits at. Scale and offset follow from the pair.
heat.levelPanel.degenerate: The two anchors share a pixel row or column, so no scale can be derived. Move them apart in both axes.
heat.levelPanel.elevationHint: Height of the map plane. Put it just under the data so nothing is hidden by it.
heat.levelPanel.libraryHint: Processed levels kept in this browser, so a decimated mesh is never rebuilt twice.
heat.levelPanel.libraryEmpty: Empty. Load a map or model, then “{button}”.
heat.levelPanel.partsHint: Guessed from part names and geometry. To change one, rename it in the source model and re-import — the split is baked into the index buffers.
heat.levelPanel.anchorPxTitle: Pixel X, from the left edge
heat.levelPanel.anchorPyTitle: Pixel Y, from the top edge
heat.measurePanel.title: Measure
heat.measurePanel.activeTitle: Left-click to drop a point, right-click to undo the last one.
heat.measurePanel.hint: Left-click drops a point, right-click removes the last. Points land on the ground plane (the map's elevation when one is loaded), so this measures across the map rather than along a line through it.
heat.measurePanel.offHint: Turn on to measure distances across the scene and read the accumulated heat under the cursor. The heat figure is the same value the colour ramp is fed, so it matches what you see.
heat.slicePanel.title: Slice
heat.slicePanel.hint: Cuts a slab out of the level and the datapoints together, so you can look inside buildings that depth occlusion is otherwise correctly hiding.
heat.slicePanel.thicknessHint: Wider than the world on one side makes it a plain cut rather than a slab.
heat.slicePanel.outsideHint: Keeping a trace of what was cut away is often easier to read than removing it outright.
heat.slicePanel.clipHeatHint: The heat is left whole, so it shows through the cut — useful for seeing what is above and below the slab you are looking at.
heat.pathPanel.resultInexact: {count, plural, one {# frame} other {# frames}} at {width}×{height}, {size} MB — {unconverged, plural, one {# frame} other {# frames}} hit the wait cap and {unconverged, plural, one {is} other {are}} not exact
heat.pathPanel.resultExact: {count, plural, one {# frame} other {# frames}} at {width}×{height}, {size} MB — every frame exact
heat.pathPanel.title: Camera path & render
heat.pathPanel.hint: Fly to a viewpoint and add it as a keyframe. The render drives the camera and the playhead together, waiting at every output frame until the picture is exact — so a flythrough comes out clean instead of carrying the sampling grain you see while moving.
heat.pathPanel.noKeys: No keyframes — a render would hold the current camera still for the whole clip, which is a perfectly good timelapse.
heat.pathPanel.goTo: Fly the camera to this keyframe
heat.pathPanel.smoothTitle: A curve through the keyframes, with the speed matched across each one so there is no lurch where two segments meet.
heat.pathPanel.straightTitle: Straight lines between keyframes. Predictable, and visibly corners at every key.
heat.pathPanel.travel: {units} units of travel — {perSecond} per second at this duration.
heat.pathPanel.noTravel: The keyframes are all in the same place, so the camera will not move.
heat.pathPanel.previewTitle: Drive the viewport camera from the path so it can be judged before rendering. Moves the playhead with it, as the render does.
heat.pathPanel.bitrateHint: Heat gradients band badly at low bitrates — there is very little detail for a codec to hide error behind.
heat.pathPanel.waitCapHint: Longest a single output frame may wait to become exact. Frames that hit it are still written, and counted in the summary.
heat.pathPanel.summary: {count, plural, one {# frame} other {# frames}} · window: {window, select, cumulative {cumulative} fixed {fixed} lifetime {lifetime} other {{window}}}
heat.pathPanel.switchesToPlay: (the render switches {all} to {play} so the playhead means something)
heat.sourcePanel.noLoadable: No loadable files in that selection.
heat.sourcePanel.title: Source
heat.sourcePanel.drop: Drop files or a folder here
heat.sourcePanel.selectionRows: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} · {size} MB · {exact, select, yes {{rows}} other {≈{rows}}} rows
heat.sourcePanel.selection: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} · {size} MB
heat.sourcePanel.positionHint: Position needs at least two of X / Y / Z. Any pair works — the unmapped axis is treated as 0 and the data is drawn as a plane inside the 3D scene, which is what a top-down map heatmap wants.
heat.sourcePanel.upAxisHint: Guessed from which axis has the smallest spread — a map is far wider than it is tall.
heat.sourcePanel.noTime: Without a time column there is no timeline: playback, windowing and lifetime are all unavailable and the view stays in {all} mode.
heat.sourcePanel.elapsedTime: This is an elapsed-time column, so every session is aligned to its own start. Good for comparing matches; use a wall-clock timestamp instead to see them in real sequence.
heat.sourcePanel.parquetTime: This column is a {format} {type} — it decodes to a real instant, so the unit setting is ignored.
heat.sourcePanel.sessionHint: One match, raid or run. This is what makes a person's samples a single track: positions are never interpolated, and trails never drawn, across a session boundary. Often a timestamp — the match's start instant, the same on every row of that match.
heat.sourcePanel.teamHint: Any low-cardinality column works as the group: it drives the colour families and the +/− split in difference mode.
heat.sourcePanel.keepHint: Retained in memory so you can filter the render live. Each numeric column costs {bytes, plural, one {# byte} other {# bytes}} per row.
heat.splitPanel.title: Difference split
heat.splitPanel.hint: Heat from the + side accumulates upward and the − side downward, so where they overlap evenly the result is zero and fully transparent. Rows on neither side are left out entirely, which is what makes a split over two of many values compare exactly those two.
heat.splitPanel.teamsHint: Assign each group to a side with the + and − buttons in the {list} list.
heat.splitPanel.columnGone: This column is no longer in the dataset.
heat.splitPanel.capped: Showing the first {shown} of {count, plural, one {# value} other {# values}}. A column this wide is better narrowed with a filter first, or split by range if its values are ordered.
heat.splitPanel.rangeHint: Range is inclusive at both ends. Values in neither range are left out, so the two ranges do not have to cover the column — {column} spans {min} to {max}.
heat.teamPanel.title: Team viewer
heat.teamPanel.interpolateTitle: When the playhead sits between two samples of the same person in the same session, place them proportionally between the two positions. Never across a session boundary — a player's last sample of one match and first of the next are hundreds of metres apart.
heat.teamPanel.sessions: Interpolation and trails join samples of one person within one session only.
heat.teamPanel.sessionsPick: Pick the session at the top of the sidebar; across a boundary the position is held and then dropped, because a player's last sample of one match and their first of the next are not one movement.
heat.teamPanel.sessionsHeld: Across a boundary the position is held and then dropped, because a player's last sample of one match and their first of the next are not one movement.
heat.teamPanel.sessionsTooMany: This load has too many matches to list, so the boundaries are still enforced but there is no session to pick.
heat.teamPanel.sharedNames: {count, plural, one {# name in this load is} other {# names in this load are}} used by more than one thing at a time — usually every AI in every match logging under one name. They are drawn as single samples, with no interpolation and no trail: a line between two of their samples would join two different creatures, not one movement.
heat.teamPanel.rawTitle: Cube per stored sample in the window rather than one interpolated cube per person. Subsampled to stay interactive.
heat.teamsList.title: Teams
heat.teamsList.differenceHint: Heat from + teams accumulates upward, heat from − teams downward. Where they overlap evenly the result is zero and fully transparent.
heat.teamsList.teamsHint: Each swatch is the colour that group draws in the heatmap. Hiding a group leaves the others where they are — the hues come from the group count, not from what is switched on, so two pictures stay comparable.
heat.viewPanel.camera.title: Camera & scene
heat.viewPanel.camera.perspectiveTitle: Natural 3D view; sprites shrink with distance
heat.viewPanel.camera.parallelTitle: No foreshortening, so equal density reads as equal size anywhere in the frame — the right choice for comparing hotspots on a map, and what makes an isometric view isometric
heat.viewPanel.camera.parallelHint: Wheel zooms — a parallel projection has no forward motion that changes scale. Switching back to {perspective} returns to the pose you left it in.
heat.viewPanel.camera.perspectiveHint: Switching to {parallel} keeps the subject the same size, so it is a change of projection rather than a jump cut.
heat.viewPanel.camera.isometricHint: True isometric: parallel projection at {pitch}°, where all three axes project to the same length. Four corners because a single one always hides half the map behind whatever is nearer.
heat.viewPanel.camera.backTitle: Return to the perspective pose you left, at the same apparent scale
heat.viewPanel.camera.fovHint: Vertical angle. Narrow flattens perspective and reads more like a parallel projection; wide exaggerates depth and is hard to judge distance in.
heat.viewPanel.camera.fovParallelHint: A parallel projection has no field of view, but this still sets the scale the switch back to {perspective} solves for, and the distance Frame uses.
heat.viewPanel.camera.flySpeedHint: Shown over the viewport too, where it can be dragged. The mouse wheel steps it by half again a notch; {shift} boosts 6×, {alt} slows to 15%.
heat.viewPanel.camera.mirrorHint: For a game whose world comes out mirrored - right-hand bends drawn as left-hand ones. Inverting X or Z fixes it; only the drawing changes, never the data or its coordinates.
heat.viewPanel.dof.title: Depth of field
heat.viewPanel.dof.hint: Applied to the level, grid and cubes — not to the heat. Heat at a pixel is the sum of sprites at many different depths, so it has no single depth to be out of focus at, and blurring it by whatever geometry sits behind it would be wrong wherever it floats in front. Sharp data over softened context is also the more useful of the two.
heat.viewPanel.dof.autoFocusTitle: Use the distance the last Frame used, which follows the data instead of needing a number.
heat.viewPanel.dof.apertureHint: Depth kept sharp, as a fraction of the focus distance. Relative rather than an f-number because these scenes span anything from a room to an eight-kilometre map.
heat.viewPanel.dof.maxBlurHint: The cost of the effect scales with this: it is a 24-tap gather at this radius, on the scene only.
heat.viewPanel.gamepad.title: Gamepad
heat.viewPanel.gamepad.none: No pad detected. Browsers only reveal a controller after it sends its first input — press a button on it.
heat.viewPanel.gamepad.hint: Left stick moves, right stick looks. Triggers rise and fall, {rb} boosts 6×, {lb} slows to 15%, {a} is a 3× sprint, {y} frames the dataset. In orthographic view the triggers zoom.
heat.viewPanel.gamepad.deadzoneHint: Radial, so a diagonal push never leaks into one axis alone. Raise it if the camera drifts when the sticks are centred.
heat.viewPanel.gamepad.curveHint: Higher gives finer control near centre while still reaching full speed at the rim.
heat.viewPanel.perf.hint: Each frame splats a stratified random subset of the visible rows with weight scaled to compensate, so the expected heat is exact at any budget. Holding the view still keeps merging frames until every row has contributed.
heat.viewPanel.perf.exactTitle: Never show the sampling grain, at the cost of frame time. A camera move throws away the accumulation, so a moving frame shows only as much of the data as that one frame drew — which is what makes moving glitter. With this on, the sprite budget below is a floor rather than a ceiling and every frame is the finished picture. Turn it off on hardware that cannot afford the whole field at once: the budget becomes a real limit again and the view converges over a few still frames instead.
heat.viewPanel.perf.exactHint: The budget below is a floor while this is on — frame cost follows the size of the data, bounded only by what one draw can carry. Narrow the time window, filter, or set a distance cull to reduce it.
heat.viewPanel.perf.adaptiveTitle: Tune sprites-per-frame automatically to hold the target framerate — and stop tuning it once that stops helping. There is no per-pass timing available, so a slow frame looks the same whether the sprites caused it or a heavy level did; if cutting to the floor still misses the target, the sprites were not the cost and the budget is raised back up rather than left starving the picture for nothing.
heat.viewPanel.perf.heatResolutionHint: Fragment cost scales with the square of this. Dropping to 50% quarters the blend work and the heat field is smooth enough that it barely shows.
heat.viewPanel.perf.progressiveTitle: Accumulate across frames while the view is static. Turn off to see the single-frame estimate.
heat.viewPanel.resources.summaryOf: Resource budgets — {ram} of {ceiling} RAM, {gpu} GPU, {cores, plural, one {# core} other {# cores}}
heat.viewPanel.resources.summary: Resource budgets — {ram} RAM, {gpu} GPU, {cores, plural, one {# core} other {# cores}}
heat.viewPanel.resources.hint: Detected automatically and used as the default. Turn one down to leave room for something else on the machine.
heat.viewPanel.resources.heldDown: The default is held down by what is free right now, not by this machine's memory.
heat.viewPanel.resources.inUse: {total} installed with {free} free, so {used} is in use by other programs — hence a default of {max} rather than {ceiling}.
heat.viewPanel.resources.hardwareAllows: The default is {max}; the hardware allows up to {ceiling}.
heat.viewPanel.resources.sliderGoesTo: The slider goes to {ceiling}. Close what you can spare and press {button} to move the default up, or raise it by hand if you know the memory will be there by the time the load runs.
heat.viewPanel.resources.capped: The RAM figure is the browser's ceiling, not this machine's. <mono>{api}</mono> is clamped to 8 GiB by {chrome} and {edge} to limit fingerprinting, so 16 GB and 256 GB both report 8 and the 60% share of it comes to {max} either way. Normally the dev server reports the real figure instead; this page did not get an answer from it. If this machine has more, say so with the slider — past {max} the number is your assertion rather than a measurement, and getting it wrong costs an out-of-memory tab crash mid-load rather than a warning.
heat.viewPanel.resources.gpuInferred: The GPU figure is inferred, not measured — no API reports VRAM to a web page at all. It is guessed from the largest texture this context admits to, which separates an integrated part from a discrete one and nothing finer, so a card with far more than {max} reads the same as one with exactly that. The slider goes to {ceiling}; raise it if you know the card.
heat.viewPanel.resources.threadsHint: Files are parsed this many at a time, each in a worker of its own, and fewer when the RAM budget has no room for another. The default leaves cores free so the page keeps repainting — an ingest that saturates every core looks like a hang even while it is progressing.
heat.viewPanel.resources.derivedCapped: No browser API reports free memory and none reports VRAM at all, so these figures are derived from what is detectable: installed RAM (which the browser rounds down and caps at 8 GiB), this tab's own heap limit, and the core count. The dev server can report the machine's real memory, and normally does — this page did not get an answer from it, so the capped guess is in use.
heat.viewPanel.resources.derivedServer: The RAM figure comes from the process serving this page, which can read the machine's real installed and free memory — the browser's own API is capped at 8 GiB and reports no free memory at all. GPU memory is still a guess: no API reports VRAM.
heat.linePanel.title: Routes
heat.linePanel.about: A line from each sample of a person to their next, with the heat falling off sideways as a sprite's falls off from its centre. It shows where people went, not where they stood.
heat.linePanel.req.noSession: none - all rows are one session
heat.linePanel.req.eventsChosen: {starts, plural, one {# start} other {# starts}}, {ends, plural, one {# end} other {# ends}}
heat.linePanel.playback: Played back, each person is a point moving between their samples and drawing the route behind them. With a fixed time window the tail fades over that window; with a cumulative one the whole route so far stays.
heat.linePanel.wholeTracks: No event column: each person's track in each session is one route, broken where the track has a gap.
heat.linePanel.startsHint: None chosen: at a person's first sample, and again after each end.
heat.linePanel.endsHint: The line runs up to the end itself. None chosen: where the person's track ends.
heat.linePanel.pointsHint: None chosen: every row of the person. Narrow it when the column also holds rows placed somewhere else, such as where a grenade landed.
heat.linePanel.more: {count, plural, one {# more value} other {# more values}} not shown
